html:
Two attempts by Kublai Khan, ruler of the Mongol Yuan dynasty, to conquer Japan, in 1274 and 1281. Both failed.

After Japan ignored his demands to submit, Kublai sent a fleet built and partly manned by Korea, which the Mongols had forced to serve them. In 1274 it landed at Hakata Bay in Kyushu. The samurai met unfamiliar tactics: massed archers, drums and exploding bombs. After a day of fighting the invaders went back to their ships, and a storm wrecked many of them.

The Japanese built a stone wall along Hakata Bay. In 1281 a far larger force came in two fleets, one from Korea and one from southern China, newly taken from the Song. The wall and raids by small boats kept it from landing in strength, and then a typhoon destroyed much of the fleet.

The Japanese called the storms kamikaze, divine winds. The cost of defence, with no land won to reward the warriors, strained the Kamakura shogunate, which fell in 1333.
sum: Two attempts by Kublai Khan, ruler of the Mongol Yuan dynasty, to conquer Japan, in 1274 and 1281. Both failed.
